newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden reiterates crown-ERM not a current issue.
newsitem.headline: Sweden reiterates crown-ERM not a current issue.

text.p: Following is a statement by Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink issued by his ministry in Stockholm on Sunday:
"The decision does not affect Sweden's position on participating in ERM.

"It is still the government's perception that it is not a current issue for Sweden to link the crown to the ERM. Since November 1992 Sweden has had a floating exchange rate. Price stability is the overriding aim for monetary and exchange rate policy. This approach has been successful and there is no reason to change it.

"The Swedish economy continues to develop positively. The public finances are strengthening rapidly and inflation is the lowest in Europe. Through this, the chances of cutting unemployment by half by the year 2000 are improved.

"Sweden has good chances of fulfilling the convergence criteria in 1997. The government and parliament will in the autumn of 1997 adopt a position on the issue of a potential Swedish participation in the currency union." -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1004
